title: Azure Networking

header.html: Describe virtual networking, including the purpose of Azure virtual networks, subnets, peering, Azure DNS, Azure VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute; Define public and private endpoints
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

toc.title: Connecting to on-premises: VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute

html:
1Azure virtual networks

An Azure virtual network (VNet) is your private, isolated network in Azure. Resources placed in it (VMs, app services with network integration, and more) can talk to each other, to the internet and to on-premises networks.

Concept Meaning
Address space The private IP range of the VNet (for example 10.0.0.0/16)
Subnet A segment of the VNet's address space; you place resources in subnets
Region A VNet lives in one region and one subscription
Isolation VNets are isolated from each other by default

A VNet provides:

  • Communication between Azure resources (privately).
  • Communication with the internet (outbound by default; inbound only if you allow it).
  • Communication with on-premises (through VPN Gateway or ExpressRoute).
  • Filtering and routing of traffic (network security groups, route tables).

Subnets let you segment a network, for example one subnet for web servers and another for databases, and apply different security rules to each.

Exam tip

. A network security group (NSG) filters traffic to and from resources in a subnet with allow and deny rules. Beyond the study guide The skills list does not name NSGs, but VM questions often mention them.

2Virtual network peering

VNet peering connects two virtual networks so resources in each can communicate privately, with low latency, over the Microsoft backbone network, not the internet.

  • Works across regions too (global VNet peering).
  • Resources use private IP addresses to reach each other.
  • Peering is non-transitive: if A peers with B and B peers with C, A and C are not connected unless you peer them as well. Beyond the study guide
Exam tip

. "Connect two Azure virtual networks privately" → VNet peering.

3Azure DNS

Azure DNS is a hosting service for DNS domains that provides name resolution using Microsoft's global network. You manage your DNS records with the same credentials, billing and tools as other Azure services.

  • Use it to host your public domain (for example fabrikam.example) and map names to IP addresses.
  • Private DNS zones resolve names inside your virtual networks.
  • Azure DNS does not sell or register domain names; it hosts the records.

4Connecting to on-premises: VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute

Azure VPN Gateway Azure ExpressRoute
Connection Encrypted tunnel over the public internet Private, dedicated connection through a connectivity provider
Goes over the internet? Yes (encrypted) No
Speed and latency Depends on the internet Higher, more predictable, lower latency
Reliability Good Higher (provider connection, redundancy)
Cost and setup Lower, quick Higher, needs a provider
Typical use Small to medium sites, remote users, backup path Large data volumes, critical or regulated workloads

VPN Gateway connection types:

  • Site-to-site: connects an on-premises network to a VNet.
  • Point-to-site: connects a single client computer to a VNet.
  • VNet-to-VNet: connects two VNets.
Exam tip

. VPN = encrypted over the internet. ExpressRoute = private line, not the internet. If the question says "does not go over the public internet", "dedicated" or "higher reliability", pick ExpressRoute.

5Public and private endpoints

Public endpoint Private endpoint
Address A public IP address reachable from the internet A private IP address from your VNet
Traffic Over the internet (can be restricted) Stays on the Microsoft backbone, inside your network
Use Services meant to be reached publicly Reach a PaaS service (storage, SQL) privately

A private endpoint is a network interface that connects you privately and securely to a service powered by Azure Private Link. It brings the service into your VNet using a private IP.

Exam tip

. "Access an Azure storage account only from the virtual network, without exposing it to the internet" → private endpoint.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors has two virtual networks in different regions and wants resources in each to talk privately over the Microsoft backbone. What should it use?

  • AAzure DNS
  • BA public endpoint
  • CA resource lock
  • DVNet peering
Show the answer

Answer: D. VNet peering connects virtual networks privately, including across regions.

S2A company needs a connection to Azure that does not travel over the public internet and offers predictable performance. What fits?

  • AAzure ExpressRoute
  • BAzure VPN Gateway
  • CAzure DNS
  • DA subnet
Show the answer

Answer: A. ExpressRoute is a private connection through a provider and does not use the public internet. VPN Gateway is encrypted but uses the internet.

S3An administrator wants to connect an on-premises office network to Azure quickly with an encrypted tunnel over the internet. What fits?

  • AVPN Gateway (site-to-site)
  • BExpressRoute
  • CA private endpoint
  • DAzure Policy
Show the answer

Answer: A. A site-to-site VPN uses an encrypted tunnel over the internet.

S4What does a private endpoint give a storage account?

  • AA public IP address reachable from the internet
  • BA second region for disaster recovery
  • CA new subscription for the service
  • DA private IP address from the virtual network
Show the answer

Answer: D. A private endpoint places a network interface with a private IP in the VNet for the service.

S5What is a subnet?

  • AA copy of a virtual network in another region
  • BA type of storage account
  • CA DNS record
  • DA segment of a virtual network's address space
Show the answer

Answer: D. Subnets divide the address space so resources can be grouped and secured separately.

S6Which service hosts DNS records and provides name resolution on Microsoft's network?

  • AAzure DNS
  • BAzure Advisor
  • CAzure Arc
  • DAzure Policy
Show the answer

Answer: A. Azure DNS hosts DNS domains and resolves names. It does not register domain names.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is a virtual network?

Show the answer

A private, isolated network in Azure.

R2What does VNet peering do?

Show the answer

Connects two virtual networks so they communicate privately over the Microsoft backbone.

R3VPN Gateway or ExpressRoute: which avoids the public internet?

Show the answer

ExpressRoute.

R4Name the three VPN Gateway connection types.

Show the answer

Site-to-site, point-to-site and VNet-to-VNet.

R5Which kind of endpoint uses a private IP address from your VNet?

Show the answer

A private endpoint.

R6Does Azure DNS register domain names?

Show the answer

No. It hosts DNS records for domains you own.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
VNet private isolated network in one region; address space split into subnets
Subnet segment of the VNet; apply separate rules
Peering connects VNets privately over the Microsoft backbone, also across regions
Azure DNS hosts DNS records and name resolution; private zones inside VNets
VPN Gateway encrypted over the internet; site-to-site, point-to-site, VNet-to-VNet
ExpressRoute private dedicated connection through a provider, not the internet
Endpoints public = public IP; private = private IP in your VNet (Private Link)
